water._doc: Water (render/shaders/water.gdshader). Ripples: the peak of the fetch-limited JONSWAP spectrum (Hasselmann et al. 1973, Dtsch. Hydrogr. Z. Suppl. A8 no. 12), f_p = 3.5 (g / U) (g X / U^2)^-0.33 with g = 9.80665 m/s2, the breeze U = 3 m/s (wind_speed_ms of the vegetation material) and X = fetch_m = 400 m, the width of a lake of the map (terrain_gen.cpp: a basin of radius 170 m, wobbling by 38 %, is 210 to 470 m across): peak_hz = 1.5399 Hz, wavelength g / (2 pi f_p^2) = 0.6582 m, wave_scale its inverse, 1.5193 cells a metre; the detail layer at twice the frequency, a quarter of the wavelength (detail_ratio 4), equal in slope by the f^-5 equilibrium range (Phillips 1958, J. Fluid Mech. 4(4)). slope_sigma 0.1355: rms of the Cox & Munk 1954 (J. Opt. Soc. Am. 44(11)) clean-surface mean square slope 0.003 + 0.00512 U = 0.01836. ripple_strength 0.1764: slope_sigma over the rms slope of the two noise layers as the shader sums them, 0.7680 (measured over 8 000 000 samples of lattice_noise.gdshaderinc). specular_f0 0.357: Godot's F0 = 0.16 SPECULAR^2 (F0() in servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl) for water's F0 ((1.333 - 1) / (1.333 + 1))^2 = 0.0204. shallow, mid, deep, foam_tint, gravel, silt, bed_from_m, silt_m, bed_cover, bed_wet, tint_depth_m, slick_share, foam_m, rim_m and bed_seen_m, bed_hidden_m, sheet_least and sheet_most: the water over its own bed, the bed showing through the first metres and the sheet closing with depth; modelling choices, checked against the 4.0 in the same frame (ports/landscape/relatorio.md). paws_m and paws_rough the gust patches that roughen the surface: modelling choices. Those are screen colours; the albedos here are what shows as them in our render: the river of capture_landscape.tscn at noon, screen (186, 210, 219) from the mean of the albedos #5783a6 and #5e788f, gives the linear gain of the light on the water through the inverse of ACES (render/tone_map.gd), (2.27, 1.98, 1.57), and each target is divided by it.

terrain._doc: Terrain (render/shaders/terrain.gdshader). past_map_y_m: Terrain3D draws a flat ground past its regions; it lies this far down, a modelling choice under the depth where the water hides its bed, so the sea is what shows past the map. detail_wide_*: how far the blades' colour stays, held to the lawn of ceu_alto with the 4.0 (edge energy 0.159 against 0.249 at 0.1 to 0.3 m a pixel before it). The shore (render/shaders/shore.gdshaderinc), modelling choices held to the river pair with the 4.0: the beach fades out between beach_from_m and beach_to_m over the water beside it, a steep bank between bank_from_m and bank_to_m, each edge wandering by its _wander_m; the band is wet from wet_to_m down to wet_from_m, keeping wet_keep of its light; shore_gentle_from and _to are 1 - cos of 24 and 40 degrees, where loose sand gives way to a cut bank. biome_dry: the dry stratum of each biome's main formation (nature.json) at a dry season of 0.55; straw_share how much of a dry patch turns to straw, the 4.0's look. grass_bump 0.8, blade_bump 1.2: the 4.0's strengths of the grass normal map and of the blades.22-0.27 through the inverse of ACES, the light on our ground being twice the albedo at noon (radiance over albedo, 2.0, 1.8, 1.5). grain_*: the speckle of the map at the pixel, the 4.0's share.0, compared by the fine contrast of the same field (standard deviation of luma under a 6 px blur: 14.5 in reference-minha/03.jpg). Slope bands as 1 - normal.y, that is 1 - cos(angle): dirt_from 0.117 = 28 deg and dirt_to 0.181 = 35 deg, loose soil shows between the low end of talus measured on Earth (28.0-33.4 deg, Kreczmer, Dabski & Zambrowska 2026, Miscellanea Geographica, doi:10.2478/mgrsd-2025-0032) and its repose angle near 35 deg (Francou & Mante 1990, Permafrost and Periglacial Processes 1(1), doi:10.1002/ppp.3430010107); rock_slope 0.234 = 40 deg, bare rock steeper than any loose debris rests.
